Nique Clifford.text: Justin Martinez: Asked Mark Daigneault about newly-acquired guard Nique Clifford: “The first thing I like is not about his game. It’s him as a guy. He’s a really, really good guy. He’s a team guy. He wants to be a part of team basketball. He wants to compete. He’s willing to earn what he gets. He’s got all of the marks of the makeup that we look for, which I think Sam (Presti) has done a great job of as we’ve layered guys in through the draft or through trade. He tries to find people who naturally align with the way that we want to be, and he does that. And I think that’s important when you have a team that has the ethos that we have established at this point.“And then as a player, there’s just a versatility to him, I think. I think he’s a guy who can defend different positions. He’s good on the ball and he’s good off the ball. He’s sound on the principles on that end of the floor. And then on offense, he can play in a system, I think. We’ll see as we go, but he seems to be a guy who can fit into what we want to do as just a plug-in guy.And, also, he’s got some secondary creation stuff that he’s shown flashes of in his career so far. He’s got a little bit of a body of work, but that’s in a different place in a different context. So, as usual, we’re gonna stay open-minded and throw him out there. He’ll declare where he’s at. Draymond Green.text: With the 6-foot-6 Green filling in at Kristaps Porzingis’ old spot for the sixth time in nine games this season during their 120-100 rout of the Miami Heat, battling the kind of big men that he says give him a bit of a “Napoleon complex” in this job born out of sheer necessity, the truth is that no one is more qualified to speak on the matter. And so he did. “Since I’ve been here on this team, it’s never been about bickering, never about ‘Shame on this guy,’ ‘Shame on that guy,’” Green told The Athletic. “We’ve never had that culture here. So the same goes for (Porzingis). No one’s sitting around bashing this guy or even worried about him, for that matter. In our minds, we’ve moved forward with the players that we have here. “(Does) everyone in here think he can help us? Of course. We know what type of player he is. ButI don’t think anyone in here is sitting around waiting on him to walk through that door. Everybody’s moved on in their mindset.”New York Times
